title: Unlock an over-centre strut by its knee to stow a radiator panel
instruction: Fold the grey radiator panel down onto its black rest pads, then let go.
context: Unlock a strut that is locked straight over centre. Loading its ends, however hard, only drives its knee further into the stop, so the knee itself has to be pushed across centre, square to the strut. Aerospace technicians (O*NET 17-3021) re-stow a deployable radiator or antenna panel on its ground fixture this way after a deployment test, and aircraft mechanics (49-3011) break a landing-gear downlock brace the same way; the same lock holds a folding table's leg brace, a stepladder spreader and a tailgate stay. Once the knee is broken nothing holds the panel, so a hand must already be on it: a honeycomb panel dropped onto its pads is damaged and has to be re-inspected. A 1 g bench analogue on a stowage fixture.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; the table top is at z 0.7475. (1) Stowage fixture, fixed: dark grey anodised aluminium, sRGB (0.26, 0.27, 0.29), 2.0 kg: a 200 x 275 x 6 mm foot plate (x 0.165 to 0.365, y -0.165 to 0.110), a 24 x 190 mm hinge pedestal with two hinge cheeks and knuckles behind a hinge line along y at x 0.330, z 0.7875 (40 mm above the table), and a 12 x 10 mm strut post at (0.210, -0.136) carrying the strut pivot B at (0.210, -0.127, 0.7875). (2) Radiator panel: aluminium honeycomb with grey thermal paint, sRGB (0.72, 0.73, 0.75), friction 0.8, 250 g: 200 mm along the hinge (y -0.100 to 0.100), 120 mm deep, 5 mm thick, starting 5 mm from the hinge line; a 30 x 25 x 5 mm grab tab on its free edge centred at y 0.060; a 14 x 13 x 5 mm strut lug on its right edge 60 mm from the hinge line. It stands open at 75 deg, leaning toward the robot (free edge at about x 0.30, z 0.908); hinge travel 0 to 80 deg. (3) Deployment strut: two yellow anodised aluminium bars, sRGB (0.93, 0.72, 0.12), 12 x 8 mm section, 59.8 mm between pins (71.8 mm overall), 15 g each, friction 0.6, beside the panel's right edge (lower link at y -0.127, upper at -0.117), from B to the panel lug at (0.314, -0.117, 0.8455). The knee joins them at (0.263, -0.122, 0.815) and sits 3 deg past straight, down and away from the robot, against its stop (knee travel -3 to 150 deg); a steel knee pin, sRGB (0.80, 0.80, 0.82), 10 mm across, sticks out 25 mm toward -y. No lock spring. (4) Rest support, fixed: grey block, sRGB (0.46, 0.48, 0.51), 0.5 kg, 70 x 170 x 28.5 mm centred at (0.250, 0.0) on the foot plate, with two black rubber rest pads, sRGB (0.05, 0.05, 0.05), friction 0.9, 20 x 24 x 3 mm at (0.235, +-0.065), tops at z 0.785, the stowed panel's underside.
scoring: Measured every control step from reset: theta = panel angle (0 on the pads, 75 locked open), the knee bend (0 straight, -3 on the lock stop, + folding), the strut's lug joint gap, and the panel's angular speed from its angle change between control steps. Whole-run record: a linkkit History updated every control step and cleared only by the simulator reset, so lifting the panel and lowering it again never clears a slam. Gates, any time in the run, give 0: the panel moved faster than 60 deg/s (a slam; the scripted demo peaks at 20 deg/s, a panel let go at 75 deg reaches about 650 deg/s), or the strut's lug joint opened more than 2 mm (the simulated strut came apart; every demo and cheat run stays at or under 0.08 mm). Ladder: 0.25 = the knee was bent 8 deg or more past straight at some time (the strut unlocked); 0.5 = the panel came down to 40 deg or below at some time; 0.75 = the panel within 2 deg of its pads at the end; 1.0 = on its pads, still (under 3 deg/s) for 1 s, and the release gate: every pad point of both grippers at least 30 mm from the fixture, panel, strut and rest support and both grippers moving under 5 mm/s for the last 1 s. Success (1.0) must hold 1 s. Real trial: a protractor on the hinge cheek for the panel angle, a video at 30 fps for the panel speed and the knee crossing centre, a top photo for the hands' clearance.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lift the panel by its tab past 75 deg until the strut is straight, let the knee drop down and away onto its stop, then lower the panel until the strut carries it at 75 deg (protractor on the hinge cheek; the knee pin rests 3 deg past straight). The fixture and the rest support are fixed on taped outlines and need no reset.
fidelity: A 1 g tabletop mock-up of a metre-scale part, not flight hardware: no microgravity or zero-g offload claimed. The panel is a rigid 250 g plate; its grab tab and the knee pin are handling features. The knee's over-centre stop is a joint limit with no lock spring: the links' weight and the panel's load hold it. The strut closes onto the panel through a PhysX loop joint (a gap over 2 mm scores 0). Pins have no play or friction. Hinge 40 mm above the table for reach.
